slides.title: Four ways to move a shape
slides.prompt: Slide. Flip. Spin. Resize. Every transformation on your exam is one of these four.

children.content: SLIDE
FLIP
SPIN
RESIZE

slides.title: Match each move to its proper name

interaction.hint: Translation slides, reflection flips, rotation spins, and enlargement resizes.

config.prompt: Drag each name onto the move it describes.

slides.title: Quick check before we dig in

interaction.hint: Three of these always keep length, angle, and orientation the same.

config.prompt: Which transformation does NOT change the size of the shape?

options.whyWrong: Enlargement is the one that changes size. The others all keep length and angle.

config.successText: Reflection, rotation and translation all keep every length and every angle. Only enlargement changes size.

visual.content:
transformation 1 of 4
Translation

Sliding the shape without turning or flipping it. Every point moves the same amount, in the same direction.

slides.title: Translation: drag the triangle anywhere
slides.prompt: Every point slides the same amount. That amount is a column vector. Drag and watch.

interaction.hint: Drag the yellow tip until the column vector reads $\begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix}$.

config.prompt: Drag until the image lands on the pink outline. Shift = $\begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix}$.
config.successText: Every point moved by $\begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix}$. That's the entire description.

interaction.hint: Add the column vector to the coordinate: top to $x$, bottom to $y$.

config.prompt: $\begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix}$ moves the blue point $P$. Tap where it lands.
config.successText: $(1 + 3,\ 5 + (-2)) = (4, 3)$. Top shifts $x$, bottom shifts $y$.

interaction.hint: Negative x means LEFT. Positive y means UP. No pink outline this time — work it out.

config.prompt: $\begin{pmatrix} -5 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$. Left $5$, up $1$. No outline this time.
config.successText: You found it without the outline. The column vector reads exactly what you slid.

slides.title: See the shift on the grid first

interaction.hint: $x$-shift = image $x$ minus object $x$. Apply only that part, leaving $y$ alone.

config.prompt: $P\ (2, -1)$ moves to $P'\ (-3, 4)$. Apply ONLY the $x$-shift to $P$. Tap where it lands.
config.successText: $x$-shift is $-3 - 2 = -5$. Now do the same for $y$ in your head: $4 - (-1) = 5$. That gives the column vector on the next slide.

slides.title: How to find a column vector
slides.prompt: Walk through the method one step at a time. Then drag the image at the end and watch the vector update.

interaction.hint: Subtract: image minus object. The order matters.

config.prompt: A point $(2, -1)$ has been translated to $(-3, 4)$. The column vector is...

options.whyWrong: You did object minus image. Always image minus object.
You used the image coordinates as the vector. The vector is the SHIFT, not the destination.
Those are the object coordinates, not the shift.

config.successText: $(-3 - 2,\ 4 - (-1)) = (-5, 5)$. Image minus object, always.

altExplain.prompt: Subtraction trick. The vector is always (image minus object). Top: $-3 - 2 = -5$. Bottom: $4 - (-1) = 5$. Vector: $\begin{pmatrix} -5 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix}$.

interaction.hint: y-component is 0. Move ONLY along the x-axis.

config.prompt: Slide by $\begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}$. The image stays at the same height.
config.successText: A zero component means no shift in that direction. Same exam logic.

interaction.hint: Both negative: left and down.

config.prompt: Slide by $\begin{pmatrix} -2 \\ -4 \end{pmatrix}$. Left by 2, down by 4. No outline.
config.successText: You're reading vectors fluently now.

slides.title: Real exam question · Cambridge w25_12 Q11(a)

interaction.hint: Both components are negative: left $5$ and down $4$.

config.prompt: Cambridge Winter 2025, Paper 12. Shape $A$ maps to shape $B$ by a translation. Slide by $\begin{pmatrix} -5 \\ -4 \end{pmatrix}$.
config.successText: Mark scheme: B1 for "Translation", B1 for $\begin{pmatrix} -5 \\ -4 \end{pmatrix}$. Full marks $= 2$.

interaction.hint: Add component by component. Order doesn't matter for two translations.

config.prompt: Translate by $\begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$, then translate by $\begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ -4 \end{pmatrix}$. What single column vector does the same job?

options.whyWrong: You multiplied $2 \times 3$ on top. Translations add, never multiply.
You subtracted instead of added.
Top should be $2 + 3 = 5$, not $1$.

config.successText: Top: $2 + 3 = 5$. Bottom: $1 + (-4) = -3$. Two translations always collapse into one.

interaction.hint: Type first, then the rule.

config.prompt: Arrange the tiles into a proper exam answer.
config.successText: “Translation by $\begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix}$.” One word, one vector, full marks.

slides.title: How an examiner wants to read a translation
slides.prompt: Word + column vector, that's it. Two marks.

visual.content:
model exam answer
Translation by \(\begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix}\)
B1 \(\cdot\) word "translation"B1 \(\cdot\) correct column vector

transformation 2 of 4
Reflection

Flipping the shape across a line, like in a mirror. The shape stays the same size, but its left and right swap.

slides.title: Reflection: drag the mirror line
slides.prompt: Every point flips to the other side of a line. Drag the yellow handles to move the mirror.

slides.title: Set the mirror to land on the pink ghost

interaction.hint: The pink ghost is directly below blue. The mirror is the horizontal axis.

config.prompt: Drag the mirror so blue reflects onto the pink outline. The mirror: $y = 0$ (the $x$-axis).
config.successText: $y = 0$ is the $x$-axis. Reflecting flips the sign of $y$ on every point.

slides.title: Now you try: reflect in $y = x$

interaction.hint: $y = x$ is the diagonal through the origin going up-right.

config.prompt: Place the mirror on $y = x$. No outline this time.
config.successText: $y = x$ swaps the two coordinates: $(x, y) \to (y, x)$.

interaction.hint: $x = 0$ is the vertical axis.

config.prompt: Place the mirror on $x = 0$ (the $y$-axis).
config.successText: $x = 0$ is the $y$-axis. Reflecting flips the sign of $x$.

interaction.hint: $y = -x$ is the OTHER diagonal through the origin (going up-left).

config.prompt: Place the mirror on $y = -x$. The diagonal that drops left to right.
config.successText: $y = -x$ swaps the coordinates and flips both signs.

slides.title: Real exam question · Cambridge w25_11 Q8(a)

interaction.hint: $x = 1$ is a VERTICAL line. Every point on it has $x$-coordinate $1$.

config.prompt: Cambridge Winter 2025, Paper 11. Triangle $A$ reflects onto triangle $B$ in the line $x = 1$. Place the mirror.
config.successText: Mark scheme: B1 for "Reflection", B1 for $x = 1$. Full marks $= 2$.

slides.title: How to find the line of reflection
slides.prompt: Given an object and its image, how do you work out where the mirror is? Step through the construction.

interaction.hint: Reflecting in $y = x$ swaps the two coordinates: $(x, y) \to (y, x)$.

config.prompt: Reflect $P\ (3, 5)$ in the yellow mirror $y = x$. Tap the image.
config.successText: Reflecting in $y = x$ just swaps the two coordinates. $(3, 5) \to (5, 3)$.

interaction.hint: Reflecting in the $x$-axis ($y = 0$) flips the sign of $y$ only.

config.prompt: Reflect the blue point $P\ (2, -4)$ in the $x$-axis. Tap where the image lands.
config.successText: $(x, y) \to (x, -y)$. Only the $y$ flips when the mirror is the $x$-axis.

interaction.hint: Imagine folding the page along each line. Which one lands blue on pink?

config.prompt: The blue triangle was reflected to land on the pink. Which mirror did it?
config.contextHtml: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 220' style='display:block;width:100%;max-width:440px;height:auto;margin:0 auto;background:#0b1118;border-radius:10px;border:1px solid #141e2a' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><defs><pattern id='qmg' x='0' y='20' width='40' height='40' patternUnits='userSpaceOnUse'><path d='M 40 0 L 0 0 0 40' fill='none' stroke='#141e2a' stroke-width='0.7'/></pattern></defs><rect width='320' height='220' fill='url(#qmg)'/><line x1='0' y1='180' x2='320' y2='180' stroke='#3a4a5a' stroke-width='1.2'/><line x1='120' y1='0' x2='120' y2='220' stroke='#3a4a5a' stroke-width='1.2'/><polygon points='160,60 240,20 200,140' fill='rgba(0,171,250,0.12)' stroke='#00abfa' stroke-width='2'/><polygon points='240,140 280,60 160,100' fill='rgba(255,70,112,0.12)' stroke='#ff4670' stroke-width='2'/></svg>

options.whyWrong: The $x$-axis flips top-bottom only. Pink would still be on the left.
The $y$-axis flips left-right only. Pink would still be near the bottom.
$y = -x$ sends the image to the bottom-right, not the top.

config.successText: $y = x$ is the diagonal through the origin going up-right.

slides.title: Words don't earn marks. Equations do.

config.prompt: Two students describe the same reflection. Which one earns the mark?

options.whyWrong: Words don't earn the mark. The examiner needs the equation of the mirror line.

config.successText: Always give the mirror as an equation: $y = x$, $y = -x$, $x = 0$, $y = 0$. Never words.

slides.title: How an examiner wants to read a reflection
slides.prompt: Word + mirror as an equation. Two marks.

visual.content:
model exam answer
Reflection in the line \(y = x\)
B1 \(\cdot\) word "reflection"B1 \(\cdot\) mirror as equation

slides.title: After a reflection, orientation reverses
slides.prompt: Lengths and angles stay the same (the image is congruent). But the labelling order flips: clockwise becomes anticlockwise.

visual.content:
object · A→B→C clockwise
→
image · A'→B'→C' anticlockwise

transformation 3 of 4
Rotation

Spinning the shape around a fixed point. To describe it: how far, which way, and where.

slides.title: Rotation: drag the centre, drag the angle
slides.prompt: Three things describe any rotation. A point to spin around, an angle to spin through, and a direction.

interaction.hint: Centre at origin. Drag the angle handle a quarter-turn anticlockwise.

config.prompt: Rotate $90°$ anticlockwise about $(0, 0)$. Match the pink outline.
config.successText: $90°$ ACW about the origin: $(x, y) \to (-y, x)$.

interaction.hint: Half a turn. Both signs flip.

config.prompt: Rotate $180°$ about the origin. Direction doesn't matter for $180°$.
config.successText: $180°$: $(x, y) \to (-x, -y)$. Opposite side, same distance.

interaction.hint: Drag the angle handle a quarter-turn the OTHER way (clockwise = negative angle).

config.prompt: Rotate $90°$ clockwise about $(0, 0)$. The image lands below the $x$-axis.
config.successText: $90°$ CW: $(x, y) \to (y, -x)$. Same magnitude, opposite direction.

interaction.hint: Drag the yellow centre to $(1, 0)$ first, then set the angle.

config.prompt: Rotate $90°$ anticlockwise about $(1, 0)$. Two things to set: centre AND angle. Match the pink outline.
config.successText: Centre $(1, 0)$, $90°$ ACW. When the centre isn't the origin you must drag BOTH.

slides.title: Real exam question · Cambridge w24_12 Q16(b)

interaction.hint: Drag the centre to $(4, 1)$ first. Then rotate the angle handle a quarter-turn the OTHER way (clockwise).

config.prompt: Cambridge Winter 2024, Paper 12. Rotate the shape $90°$ clockwise about $(4, 1)$.
config.successText: Mark scheme: B1 "Rotation", B1 "$90°$ clockwise", B1 centre $(4, 1)$. Full marks $= 3$.

slides.title: How to find the centre of a 90° rotation
slides.prompt: Given an object and its 90° rotated image, find the centre using perpendicular bisectors. Two bisectors meet at the centre.

slides.title: How to find the centre of a 180° rotation
slides.prompt: For 180°, the centre is just the midpoint of any vertex-image pair. No bisectors needed.

slides.title: What three things describe a rotation?

interaction.hint: Where to spin around, how far, which way.

config.prompt: A rotation is fully described by THREE things. They are...

options.whyWrong: Mirror lines are for reflections, not rotations.
Scale factor is for enlargements, not rotations.
Column vectors are for translations. Rotations have a centre, not a vector.

config.successText: Centre + angle + direction. Drop any one of those and you lose a mark.

interaction.hint: Centre is where it spun around. Angle is how far. Direction is which way.

config.prompt: Fill in the three slots from the tiles below.
config.contextHtml: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' style='display:block;width:100%;max-width:440px;height:auto;margin:0 auto;background:#0b1118;border-radius:10px;border:1px solid #141e2a' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><defs><pattern id='rlg' x='0' y='0' width='40' height='40' patternUnits='userSpaceOnUse'><path d='M 40 0 L 0 0 0 40' fill='none' stroke='#141e2a' stroke-width='0.7'/></pattern><marker id='rlarr' viewBox='0 0 10 10' refX='9' refY='5' markerWidth='6' markerHeight='6' orient='auto-start-reverse'><path d='M 0 0 L 10 5 L 0 10 z' fill='#ff822c'/></marker></defs><rect width='320' height='200' fill='url(#rlg)'/><line x1='0' y1='160' x2='320' y2='160' stroke='#3a4a5a' stroke-width='1.2'/><line x1='160' y1='0' x2='160' y2='200' stroke='#3a4a5a' stroke-width='1.2'/><path d='M 200 120 A 56.6 56.6 0 0 0 120 120' fill='none' stroke='#ff822c' stroke-width='1.4' stroke-dasharray='4 3' marker-end='url(#rlarr)'/><polygon points='200,120 280,120 240,40' fill='rgba(0,171,250,0.12)' stroke='#00abfa' stroke-width='2'/><polygon points='120,120 120,40 40,80' fill='rgba(255,70,112,0.12)' stroke='#ff4670' stroke-width='2'/><circle cx='160' cy='160' r='5' fill='#fff067' stroke='#0b1118' stroke-width='2'/></svg>
config.successText: Rotation, $90°$ anticlockwise, centre $(0, 0)$.

interaction.hint: A full turn is $360°$. Subtract from a full turn to flip direction.

config.prompt: A rotation of $90°$ clockwise gives the same image as which anticlockwise rotation?

options.whyWrong: That's the same magnitude but opposite direction. Image would land in a different place.
$180°$ goes too far. $90°$ clockwise is $90°$ short of a full turn anticlockwise.
That's still clockwise. We need an anticlockwise equivalent.

config.successText: $360° - 90° = 270°$. Both ways describe the same image and either is accepted.

altExplain.prompt: A full turn is $360°$. Going clockwise by $90°$ lands at the same image as going anticlockwise the long way round: $360° - 90° = 270°$ anticlockwise. Same image, opposite direction name.

interaction.hint: $90°$ anticlockwise about the origin: $(x, y) \to (-y, x)$.

config.prompt: Rotate the blue point $P\ (3, 0)$ by $90°$ anticlockwise about the origin. Tap the image.

interaction.hint: Direction doesn't matter for $180°$. Both signs flip.

config.prompt: A rotation of $180°$ about the origin sends $(x, y)$ to...
config.contextHtml: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 180' style='display:block;width:100%;max-width:380px;height:auto;margin:0 auto;background:#0b1118;border-radius:10px;border:1px solid #141e2a' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><defs><pattern id='r180g' x='0' y='0' width='30' height='30' patternUnits='userSpaceOnUse'><path d='M 30 0 L 0 0 0 30' fill='none' stroke='#141e2a' stroke-width='0.7'/></pattern></defs><rect width='320' height='180' fill='url(#r180g)'/><line x1='0' y1='90' x2='320' y2='90' stroke='#3a4a5a' stroke-width='1.2'/><line x1='160' y1='0' x2='160' y2='180' stroke='#3a4a5a' stroke-width='1.2'/><line x1='70' y1='150' x2='250' y2='30' stroke='#fff067' stroke-width='1.2' stroke-dasharray='4 3'/><circle cx='250' cy='30' r='6' fill='#00abfa'/><text x='264' y='28' fill='#00abfa' font-family='Geist Mono,monospace' font-size='13' font-weight='700'>P</text><circle cx='70' cy='150' r='6' fill='#ff4670'/><text x='44' y='158' fill='#ff4670' font-family='Geist Mono,monospace' font-size='13' font-weight='700'>P'</text><circle cx='160' cy='90' r='4.5' fill='#fff067' stroke='#0b1118' stroke-width='1.5'/></svg>

options.whyWrong: That's a reflection in $y = x$, not a rotation.
Only $x$ flipped. That's a reflection in the $y$-axis.
Only $y$ flipped. That's a reflection in the $x$-axis.

config.successText: $180°$: both signs flip. The image lands on the opposite side of the centre, same distance away.

slides.title: Three rotations about the origin
slides.prompt: These three rules cover almost every rotation question on your exam. Memorise them.

visual.content:
\(90°\) anticlockwise
\((x, y) \to (-y, x)\)
\(180°\) (either way)
\((x, y) \to (-x, -y)\)
\(90°\) clockwise
\((x, y) \to (y, -x)\)

config.prompt: Two students describe the same rotation. Which one earns full marks?

options.whyWrong: No direction. Clockwise or anticlockwise? Mark scheme needs all three.

config.successText: Centre + angle + direction. All three or zero marks.

slides.title: How an examiner wants to read a rotation
slides.prompt: Word + angle + direction + centre. All three pieces, all three marks.

visual.content:
model exam answer
Rotation, \(90°\) anticlockwise, centre \((0,\ 0)\)
B1 \(\cdot\) word "rotation"B1 \(\cdot\) angle + directionB1 \(\cdot\) centre

transformation 4 of 4
Enlargement

Stretching or shrinking the shape away from a fixed point. The only move that changes size.

slides.title: Enlargement: centre and scale factor
slides.prompt: Two things define an enlargement. A point to scale from, and the scale factor.

interaction.hint: Distances from the centre double when $k = 2$.

config.prompt: Drag the pink handle until $k = 2$. Centre stays at $(0, 0)$.
config.successText: $k = 2$: every distance from the centre doubled.

interaction.hint: One-and-a-half times the distance. No outline this time.

config.prompt: Scale by $k = 1.5$ from the centre at $(0, 0)$. No pink outline this time.
config.successText: $k = 1.5$. Half again as big as the original.

interaction.hint: When the centre is the origin, multiply both coordinates by $k$.

config.prompt: Enlarge the blue point $P\ (2, 1)$ from the origin with $k = 3$. Tap the image.
config.successText: $(3 \cdot 2,\ 3 \cdot 1) = (6, 3)$. From the origin, every coordinate scales by $k$.

altExplain.prompt: When the centre is the origin, the rule is the simplest possible: multiply each coordinate of $P$ by $k$. $P\ (2, 1)$ with $k = 3$ becomes $(2 \times 3,\ 1 \times 3) = (6, 3)$. Then tap that square on the grid.

slides.title: Can scale factor be less than 1?

interaction.hint: Distances halve and the image gets smaller, but it's still called an enlargement.

config.prompt: Shrink the image to half size: $k = \tfrac{1}{2}$. Still an enlargement.
config.successText: $k = \tfrac{1}{2}$ is an enlargement too. The word covers shrinking as well as growing.

interaction.hint: Lengths scale by $k$. Areas scale by $k^2$ — square the scale factor.

config.prompt: After an enlargement with scale factor $\tfrac{1}{2}$, the image area is...
config.contextHtml:
side 2
side 1 (k = ½)

options.whyWrong: Half is what happens to lengths. Areas use $k^2 = \tfrac{1}{4}$.

options.text: one quarter of the object area

options.whyWrong: Both wrong direction and wrong factor.
Only if $k = 1$. Here $k = \tfrac{1}{2}$, so area must change.

config.successText: Areas scale by $k^2$. $\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 = \tfrac{1}{4}$. Volume would be $k^3 = \tfrac{1}{8}$.

altExplain.prompt: Think of a square. Side length $L$ becomes $kL$. Area was $L \times L = L^2$, now $kL \times kL = k^2 L^2$. So area multiplies by $k^2$, not by $k$. For $k = \tfrac{1}{2}$, area becomes $\tfrac{1}{4}$ of the original.

slides.title: Negative $k$ flips through the centre
slides.prompt: A negative scale factor sends the image to the OPPOSITE side of the centre, then scales it. $k = -2$ is twice the size, on the other side.

interaction.hint: Same size, opposite side of the centre. Push the handle just past the centre.

config.prompt: Set $k = -1$. Same size as the object, opposite side of $(0, 0)$.
config.successText: $k = -1$ is the same as a $180°$ rotation about the centre. Same size, flipped.

interaction.hint: Drag the centre to $(1, 0)$. Then set the scale factor to $-\tfrac{1}{2}$ (negative, half-size).

config.successText: Mark scheme: B1 "Enlargement", B1 centre $(1, 0)$, B1 scale factor $-\tfrac{1}{2}$. Full marks $= 3$.

interaction.hint: Type first, then the rule. Scale factor goes before centre.

config.successText: “Enlargement, scale factor $2$, centre $(1, 1)$.” Three pieces, three marks.

two moves in a row
Combining moves

Doing one move, then another. The two together often make a single, different move.

slides.title: Combining: do one, then another
slides.prompt: Two transformations in a row. The result is often a different transformation than you'd guess.

interaction.hint: Try translate-then-rotate versus rotate-then-translate. Different landing spots.

config.prompt: You do one move and then another. Does the ORDER you do them in matter?

options.whyWrong: Try rotate $90°$ then translate vs translate then rotate. They land in different places.
Most pairs depend on order. Translations are the special exception.

options.text: matters: doing A then B usually gives a different image than B then A

options.whyWrong: Order matters across most pairs of transformations.

config.successText: Order almost always matters. Two translations are the one exception (you can add their vectors in either order).

interaction.hint: Two reflections undo the flip. So no flip remains in the final image.

config.prompt: Reflect in one mirror, then reflect in a second mirror that is PARALLEL to the first. The single move that does the same thing is...

options.whyWrong: Rotations come from intersecting mirrors, not parallel ones.
Two reflections flip twice — no flip remains.
Sizes don't change under any reflection. No enlargement possible.

config.successText: Two parallel mirrors slide the shape by twice the gap between them. A translation.

slides.title: Set up two perpendicular mirrors
slides.prompt: Use the preset chips to place mirror 1 on $y = 0$ and mirror 2 on $x = 0$. Watch the final image — it's a $180°$ rotation about the origin, made entirely from two reflections.

interaction.hint: Where the mirrors cross is special — it's the only point both reflections leave alone.

config.prompt: Reflect in one mirror, then reflect in a second mirror that CROSSES the first. The single move that does the same thing is...

options.text: a rotation about the intersection point

options.whyWrong: Translations come from parallel mirrors. Intersecting mirrors give rotation.
Reflections never change size.
The angle is TWICE the angle between the mirrors, not always $180°$.

config.successText: The angle of rotation is twice the angle between the two mirrors.

interaction.hint: $y = 0$ and $y = x$ cross at the origin. Angle between them is $45°$. Double it.

config.prompt: Reflect in $y = 0$, then reflect in $y = x$. What single move does the same thing?

options.text: a rotation $90°$ clockwise about the origin
options.whyWrong: Reversing the mirror order would flip the direction. Here it's $y=0$ first, then $y=x$, which gives anticlockwise.

options.text: a rotation $90°$ anticlockwise about the origin

options.whyWrong: Parallel mirrors would give a translation. These two mirrors intersect at the origin.
Two reflections never give another reflection. The image flips an even number of times overall.

config.successText: $45°$ between the mirrors. Doubled gives $90°$. Direction is from $y=0$ toward $y=x$: anticlockwise.

altExplain.prompt: Two intersecting mirrors always give a rotation about the point where they cross. The angle of the rotation is TWICE the angle between the mirrors. $y = 0$ and $y = x$ cross at the origin and make a $45°$ angle, so the rotation is $90°$. Direction sweeps from the first mirror to the second — here that's anticlockwise.

slides.title: Two parallel mirrors give a translation

interaction.hint: Vector is twice the perpendicular gap, from the first mirror to the second.

config.prompt: Reflect in $y = 0$, then reflect in $y = 1$. What single move does the same thing?

options.whyWrong: Parallel mirrors give a translation, not a rotation.
Two reflections never give a third reflection.
Reflections don't change size, so no enlargement.

config.successText: Gap is $1$ unit, doubled gives $2$. Direction is from $y=0$ up to $y=1$: positive $y$.
